messages:
miguel: Quick sync — product asked for a console "delta export" that produces per-route heatmaps for request/response characteristics (latency, sample-rate, PII-risk buckets) but with zero PII. Two approaches on the table: 1) server-side pre-scrub + full heatmap rows, 2) export only aggregated histograms (no sample-level rows). Which do folks prefer?

sasha: Curious about scale — how big would these exports be? we already see large CSVs when customers pull logs.

emma: If we do pre-scrub, we need a strict scrub policy+audit trail. Scrubbing is nontrivial (attachments, embeddings). I'd rather we avoid sample-level rows unless strictly aggregated.

alex: +1 on aggregated. We can provide per-route percentile buckets and counts per PII-risk class. That satisfies analytics and keeps attack surface small.

maria: Quotas: exports will count against telemetry export quota? product expects a daily snapshot endpoint. If aggregated, it's cheap. If pre-scrubbed rows, that could blow quotas and S3 costs.

ori: UX note — product wants a toggle in the route page that says "Export privacy-safe heatmap". They also want a preview in the console. Preview should be very limited (one-page sample) and not surface original text.

miguel: Security perspective?

security-bot: Automated check: pre-scrubbed rows still retain structural patterns (timestamps, IP-like tokens). If you go that route, we require deterministic redaction and k-anonymity checks. Aggregated histograms avoid most of this.

alex: Technical sketch for aggregated export:
```
{
  route: "/v1/generate",
  window: "2026-03-20T00:00Z/2026-03-20T23:59Z",
  metrics: {
    latency_buckets: [0-10ms, 10-50ms, 50-200ms, 200ms+],
    token_count_hist: [0-10,11-50,51-200],
    pii_risk_counts: {low: 1200, med: 45, high: 2}
  }
}
```
This is small and safe.

emma: And we should document the PII risk classifier thresholds and version it. If customers ask "how did you flag this high?" we need an explainer.

miguel: Devex asks for a single-line flag in the config to enable the export endpoint. Proposed config snippet:
```
telemetry.exports.heatmap.enabled = true
telemetry.exports.heatmap.aggregate_only = true  # default
telemetry.exports.heatmap.retention_days = 30
```
We can add `aggregate_only=false` behind an enterprise-only feature flag but default to true.

devex-bot: note saved: add UI toggle + preview mock + API for aggregated export.

maria: Regarding quotas: if we do aggregated, let's set a daily export cost bucket of 1 export = X telemetry units. I'll draft numbers.

alex: One more thought — we might let customers select a nondeterministic downsample of raw pre-scrubbed rows for enterprise with explicit legal sign-off. That should be gated.

security-bot: Gate + audit trail + retention shorter (7 days) for any raw-rows export. Require KMS-wrapped tokens and approval.

ori: UX: if aggregated export is the default, the console preview should show a small heatmap and a CTA "Request raw sample (enterprise only)" which leads to a ticket flow. Keeps us safe and product-friendly.

miguel: Action items I heard: 1) implement aggregated export API + console preview (owner: alex), 2) telemetry config flag + default true (owner: miguel), 3) doc the PII classifier + versions (owner: emma), 4) quota pricing unit for export (owner: maria), 5) draft gated enterprise flow for raw pre-scrubbed export (owner: alex + security). I'll open an RFC.

alex: I'll put an API PR draft up — will include histogram schema and example.

emma: I'll start the classifier doc and include failure cases.

maria: I'll model cost impact and propose telemetry units.

ori: I'll mock the console preview in Figma and share.

oncall-bot: deploy-check queued for telemetry service (CI job #8912).

miguel: Thanks all — want to keep the default conservative (aggregate-only) and track feature requests for raw exports. If anyone objects to the plan, speak now or I'll file the RFC in #rfc-tracking. :thumbsup:
